text: Notebook out, pencil down — for now. {sender} starts warm: the early years, the first break, the picture everyone loves. This is the part of the dance where nobody steps on anybody.

reads.unreadable: Professional friendliness, wall to wall. What is behind it stays behind it.
reads.likely: Friendly — but the pencil is a little too ready.
reads.clear: The warmth is real and so is the agenda. Both are on the table.
reads.certain: You can see the article's structure in their eyes: three kind paragraphs, then the knife, then absolution — if you earn it.

choices.label: Give them real color — safe stories with texture
Trade warmth for warmth — open the family album

effects.text: Let them past the press kit — rare, and remembered.

text: Two topics off the record, photo approval, quotes checked. {sender} agrees — and respects you more for asking properly.
You ask for too much and get the professional smile that means: noted, and no. The pencil hovers a little closer now.
Then, without a change of tone: "And the private side? Readers keep asking what {client} goes home to." There it is — the question the whole afternoon was built around.

choices.label: Name the trap out loud, almost amused

text: Because you opened a real door, the private question arrives gently — almost an invitation rather than an ambush.

choices.label: Smile and close the album at the right page

text: You answer with a story that feels intimate and reveals nothing. {sender} knows exactly what you did — and writes it down as charm.

effects.text: handled the private question like a professional

choices.label: Wrap the sitting on a high note

text: Honesty, measured by the tablespoon. It costs a little privacy and buys a lot of credibility.

effects.text: Gave a straight answer when dodging was easier.

text: "You noticed," says {sender}, genuinely pleased, and draws a line through half a page. Games are more fun with someone who can see the board.

effects.text: sees through an ambush question instantly

text: The deflection comes out half a beat too fast, and the silence afterwards is the sound of a headline being born.

effects.text: gets nervous when the questions turn personal

text: Four columns, above the fold, and a photograph that makes the studio switchboard light up. The town reads the portrait over coffee — and reads your fingerprints nowhere in it, which is the highest compliment.

effects.text: The big portrait: {client}, at home in the spotlight
The portrait of {client} lands — warm, wide-read, on message.

text: The portrait runs — with one paragraph that reads like a raised eyebrow. Nothing actionable. Everything memorable.

effects.text: Between the lines: what is {client}'s camp not saying?
The portrait paragraph everyone underlined: something about {client}'s private life is being managed.
The portrait of {client} lands a bruise nobody can quite point to.

text: "Start at the beginning," says {sender}. "Sunset Boulevard, the first office, the first client who said yes." The warm-up lap — even the warm-up is on the record.

reads.unreadable: You cannot tell if this is a profile or a prosecution. The notebook looks the same either way.
reads.likely: Curious, mostly. There is an angle here somewhere, still folded up.
reads.clear: They came with a thesis about your agency. The interview is the search for quotes to hang it on.
reads.certain: You can read the working title in their posture — and it is only flattering if you make it so today.

choices.label: Read what angle they are really after

text: Halfway through your anecdote you see the shape of their piece: power, not glamour. Who owes whom in this town. You adjust every sentence that follows.

choices.label: Feed the thesis on your terms

text: You misjudge the piece — you play glamour while they hunt structure. Two of your best lines die in the margin, unused.

choices.label: Catch up to the real conversation

text: Then the real question, delivered like a compliment: "People say no agency closes doors as quietly as yours. Whose favor are you spending when you do that?"

choices.label: Answer without naming a single name
Own the method: discretion is the product
Turn it around: ask what they would print

text: The favor question comes — and you have been building the answer for ten minutes. You give them power as craft, not conspiracy.
A whole paragraph about discretion, containing none. {sender} laughs once, writes twice.

effects.text: talks for an hour and leaks nothing

text: "Discretion is the product." You watch the sentence land and know it will be the pull quote. Good. It is even true.

effects.text: Gave the quote of the piece, on purpose.

text: "What would YOU print?" The tables turn for exactly one round — long enough to learn what they have, which is less than they implied.

choices.label: Trade the last question for goodwill

text: One clause too many. Nothing quotable against you — but enough for a footnote with teeth, and journalists build careers out of footnotes.

effects.text: almost names names when flattered

choices.label: End the hour before it gets worse

text: The piece runs on a Sunday: the agency as craft, the manager as its quiet architect. Three rival agents call it puffery. All three keep the clipping.

effects.text: Profile: how {agency} builds careers without raising its voice
The agency profile lands exactly the way you steered it.

text: The profile runs with one sentence you will be asked about at every dinner for a month. Not fatal. Just permanent.

effects.text: The agency piece: {agency}, and the doors it closes so quietly
The agency profile carries an edge you did not order.

text: No warm-up this time. {sender} lays the rumor on the table between you, still folded, like a hand of cards. "I have enough to print something. Help me print the right thing."

reads.unreadable: Impossible to say how much they actually have. That is, of course, the technique.
reads.likely: They have something — the confidence is not entirely theater.
reads.clear: They have less than they claim. The bluff is load-bearing.
reads.certain: You can count their cards from here: one source, secondhand, and a deadline that is doing most of the pushing.

choices.label: Trade: bury this one, and I owe you better

text: Twenty minutes of warm, useless sentences. {sender} hangs up with pages of nothing and a grudging smile you can hear.

effects.text: cannot be cracked on the phone

text: One denial too specific — you correct a detail they never mentioned. The silence on the line is the sound of a note being made.

effects.text: denies details nobody asked about

text: "Better, and exclusive?" — "Better, and exclusive." The rumor goes into a drawer. The drawer has a price tag, and your name is on the invoice.
"Everyone offers me a better story," says {sender}. "Nobody ever has one by Friday." The pencil is moving again. One more chance to change what it writes.

choices.label: Give one careful quote on the record

text: You slide a different story across the table — smaller, true, and printable tomorrow. Journalists are hungry animals; the nearest meal usually wins.
The column runs that week about somebody else entirely. Stories are fires: this one found no oxygen at your door.

effects.text: The fishing expedition comes up empty. The rumor loses a week of air.

text: The piece runs with the phrase "sources close to the agency" — which is you, badly translated. The rumor gains a byline.

effects.text: Column: the story {agency} did not want to discuss
The press call goes sideways — the rumor now has ink behind it.

text: The rumor stays out of print, and a journalist now holds your marker. In this town that is not a debt — it is a subscription.

effects.text: A story is buried, a debt is born. The ledger of favors turns a page.

text: One sentence, polished for an hour, printed in the morning. It neither confirms nor denies — it reframes. Damage: contained, not canceled.

effects.text: On the record: {agency} addresses the whispers, briefly
Your one careful quote takes the edge off the story — most of it.

text: Tomorrow's column belongs to the story you fed it. The one you feared keeps breathing, quieter, in the back room.

effects.text: Exclusive: a story from the {agency} orbit — not the one you heard
Traded a better story to keep a worse one dark.
A swap at the news desk: your story dies, another lives.
